snippet.title: Commodore 64 Longplay [045] Hook (EU)
snippet.description:
http://www.longplays.org

Played by: MadMatty

Hook, developed by Painting by Numbers and published by ocean in 1992

“Peter Pan has grown up, and is far away from Neverland, Captain Hook has not forgotten and schemes his revenge.  Kidnapping Peters children, he lures our hero back to the Island of Pirates and “Lost Boys” for a final confrontation.  With the help of Tinkerbell the faithful fairy, you take on the role of Peter in this magic adventure fraught with danger and excitement.”

A late release on the Commodore 64.  One of the last few games I got before moving onto the Amiga.  This version of the game was also made for the Gameboy and Nes.  I was disappointed it wasn't like the Amiga point and click game at the time.  I do not know which version came first but the game does have an overall console game design in the way it is presented.  The game was converted to many different platforms of the time by different developer groups and while they share the same design goal, some versions come out quite different.

The game is mostly platforming and not overly challenging.  You get map screen where you can choose to do levels in a different order and completing levels unlocks more locations to select.  Between levels you might have a flying level where you can collect balloons but dodge dynamite.  Some levels involve diving for treasure.  Collecting a thimble allows you to attract tinkerbell who will fly out and destroy enemies. It is a limit use power however.  You can also find a sword to help kill enemies.  Marbles are also required to reveal hidden paths shown by pixie dust.

Some later levels involve going underground and you can collect a metal detector.  Going around the level with the detector can reveal hidden treasure to boost your score.

Overall the game is quite large and well presented taking well over an hour to complete.  A minor niggle is that the viewport is quite small leaving wasted screen space.  The map screen does fill it though.  It's also one that would have actually benefited from a cartridge release due to all its levels and loading but ocean had given up with the format by this time.
